etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin pyrrhichius (“dibrach”), from πυρρίχη (purrhíkhē, “war dance”), from πυρρός (purrhós, “flame-colored, red”), from πῦρ (pûr, “fire”).
senses: (prosody) Of or characterized by pyrrhics (metrical feet with two short syllables).
(Ancient Greece) Relating to Pyrrhus, a Macedonian king, or some of his costly victories he had while fighting Rome.
(prosody) A metric foot with two short or unaccented syllables.
